holidays.name: International Joke Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to telling jokes, puns, and groan-worthy one-liners to anyone within earshot. Dad jokers everywhere are encouraged to run wild, and the worse the pun, the better.
holidays.origin: Established by humorist Wayne Reinagel, founder of the Humor Institute, to encourage people to lighten up and share laughter at the start of summer.
holidays.funFact: The oldest known joke is a Sumerian proverb about flatulence, dating back to around 1900 BCE, proving that potty humor has always been a classic.

holidays.name: Canada Day
holidays.description: Canada's national holiday, packed with fireworks, parades, red-and-white outfits, and plenty of poutine. It is a day when Canadians celebrate the country with maple-flavored enthusiasm and backyard barbecues.
holidays.origin: Originally called Dominion Day, it commemorates the 1867 enactment of the Constitution Act, which united Canada's colonies into a single federation. It was renamed Canada Day in 1982.
holidays.funFact: July 1 is also known as 'Moving Day' in Quebec, when most residential leases end and thousands of people relocate all at once, leaving streets full of couches and boxes.

holidays.name: Ice Cream Sandwich Day
holidays.description: A day to enjoy the perfect marriage of creamy frozen ice cream pressed between two soft cookies or wafers. It is an unofficial excuse to eat dessert in the summer heat.
holidays.origin: This unofficial food holiday grew out of the popularity of the frozen treat, which is said to have been sold by pushcart vendors in New York City in the late 1800s.
holidays.funFact: In Singapore, street vendors sell ice cream served between slices of plain bread, a tradition that is still going strong today.

holidays.name: National Gingersnap Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the spicy, crunchy cookie that has been dunked in coffee and milk for centuries. Bakers and cookie lovers alike enjoy a snap of ginger zing.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance celebrating the traditional ginger-flavored cookie, which descends from medieval European gingerbread recipes.
holidays.funFact: Queen Elizabeth I is credited with popularizing gingerbread by having it shaped into likenesses of visiting dignitaries.

holidays.name: Zip Code Day
holidays.description: A day to appreciate those five little digits that help your mail find its way. It honors the humble postal code and the system that sorts billions of letters.
holidays.origin: The United States Post Office Department introduced ZIP codes on July 1, 1963, to speed up mail sorting and delivery.
holidays.funFact: ZIP stands for Zone Improvement Plan, and the mascot of the program was a cartoon character named Mr. ZIP who appeared on stamps and mailings.
